clue.text: City hit by our artillery

indicators.note: the thing struck comes after the striker, so the second part stands beside the first

parts.note: the Royal Artillery, Britain's own gunners
to bat is to hit, as with a cricket bat

explanation.surface: A town is shelled by our own guns.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay reads backwards from the surface: the striking word comes after the gunners that do it.
explanation.definitionFit: Rabat is the capital of Morocco, on its Atlantic coast.

clue.text: Parliamentary supporter's blunt point

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a Puritan on Parliament's side in the English Civil War, named for cropped hair
second meaning: a tip that is rounded rather than sharp, like a dull screw or nail

explanation.walkthrough: The 's is a link: the supporter is the blunt point.
explanation.definitionFit: Cromwell's followers were mocked for close-cropped hair, and a rounded tip on a screw bears the same description literally.

clue.text: Report about hard drug

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: a report is the loud noise of a gun
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A news report about a hard drug.
explanation.walkthrough: Hard drug reads as one phrase, but hard belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Bhang is a preparation of cannabis leaves used in India, a narcotic.

clue.text: Wretched traitor caught by soldiers in restaurant

indicators.note: something caught by others is held between them

parts.note: the Territorial Army, Britain's reserve force

indicators.note: wretched means in a sorry state, so the word is knocked out of shape

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Troops arrest a despicable turncoat in a restaurant.
explanation.definitionFit: A trattoria is a simple Italian eatery serving homely food.

clue.text: Underpublicized novel?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: never reported, so nobody has been told of it
second meaning: without precedent, never encountered before

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark invites a book that sold poorly; the novel here is the adjective for something new.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes something nobody has been told about, and also something so new it lacks any precedent.

clue.text: Remove rider's new horn, in practice

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: custom or habit

indicators.note: new suggests a fresh version, so the letters take a different order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A rider trains with a new hunting horn.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is a link: the definition is followed by is.
explanation.definitionFit: To unhorse is to throw or knock a rider off their mount, as in a joust.

clue.text: Reveal all? To us, that's terrible

parts.note: to reveal all is to hide nothing, and nothing is O
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone baring everything strikes us as shocking.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the reversal of sense: revealing all means hiding nothing, zero being O.
explanation.definitionFit: Something hideous is frightful and ugly, dreadful to look at.

clue.text: Opposition is supporting model worker

indicators.note: in a down answer, supporting means sitting underneath, so this piece comes second

parts.note: the ant is the proverbial example of industry
taken as written

explanation.surface: The opposition backs an exemplary employee.
explanation.definitionFit: Antis are people against something, a body of opponents.

clue.text: Find dancing event jolly

parts.note: a party with dancing to recorded music
in British slang jolly means very, as in jolly good

explanation.surface: Someone finds a dance a jolly occasion.
explanation.definitionFit: Find as a noun is something found, a discovery made.

clue.text: Honest old German

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a member of the Germanic people who conquered Gaul

explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means open and sincere, and the noun names one of the ancient Germanic tribe that gave France its name.

clue.text: Girl struck without shame

parts.note: a girl's name
hit hard

explanation.surface: A young woman is hit and feels no embarrassment about it.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unabashed is not embarrassed or abashed in the slightest, acting boldly and openly.

clue.text: From area round Firenze, take an operatic heroine

indicators.note: to take something from a word is to subtract it, leaving the rest behind

parts.note: the Italian name of Tuscany, the region around Florence (Firenze in Italian)
taken as written, and removed

explanation.surface: Someone takes an opera heroine from the Florence region, apt since Puccini was Tuscan.
explanation.definitionFit: Tosca is the title role of Puccini's opera, the singer Floria Tosca.

clue.text: Spade I dealt, finally, as part of hand

parts.note: spade used as a verb: to turn over soil
taken as written

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word just before it

parts.note: the last letter of dealt

explanation.surface: A card player is dealt a spade as part of a hand of cards.
explanation.walkthrough: Spade, dealt and hand all set up a card table; spade is really a verb for turning soil.
explanation.definitionFit: A digit is a finger or thumb, one of the parts that make up a hand.

clue.text: Turn over ground to handle this part of plant

parts.note: pigs root when they turn over soil with their snouts
the stock is the handle of a gun or whip

explanation.surface: A gardener digs the soil before handling a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A rootstock is the underground stem or the rooted base onto which a gardener grafts another variety.

clue.text: Grenade exploded in defensive position

indicators.note: something exploded is blown apart, its letters scattered into a fresh order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A grenade goes off near troops dug in for defence.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is French, a fencing call.
explanation.definitionFit: A fencer calls this to warn an opponent to take the guard stance, ready to parry.

clue.text: Red Sea and this region couldn't be more different

definitions.text: Red Sea and this region couldn't be more different

parts.words: Red Sea and this region couldn't be more different
parts.note: surface reading: a hot Middle Eastern sea against some contrasting place
setter's reading: swap each word of the first name for its opposite, colour for colour and water for dry ground

explanation.walkthrough: Red and green are traffic-light opposites, and sea is the opposite of land.
explanation.definitionFit: The Arctic island is the literal word-by-word opposite of the Middle Eastern sea's name.

clue.text: Paper on left part of balance is naturally a little light

indicators.note: placed at the left means the first piece is written before the second

parts.note: The Sun is a British daily newspaper
the beam is the crossbar of a pair of scales, from which the pans hang

explanation.surface: A newspaper on a scale pan barely registers, since paper is light.
explanation.walkthrough: Light seems to be about weight on the scales; it is daylight.
explanation.definitionFit: A sunbeam is a single ray of sunshine, a small amount of natural daylight.

clue.text: Fluid line ordered for invalid

definitions.note: past participle used as an adjective: made invalid

indicators.note: ordered means put into a new sequence, so the letters are arranged afresh

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A patient is prescribed a drip line.
explanation.walkthrough: Invalid suggests a sick person; it is the adjective meaning void.
explanation.definitionFit: Something nullified has been cancelled, declared void and of no legal force.

clue.text: Placer of explosives in pit stratum?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a ship that lays sea mines
second meaning: read literally, a seam or level in a colliery

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the second meaning splits the word in two.
explanation.definitionFit: A naval vessel sows explosive charges at sea, and a colliery level read word by word is the same compound.

clue.text: Old-fashioned type, long with firm

parts.note: to long for something is to be dying for it
solid, not soft

explanation.surface: A traditionalist who has long been with the same company.
explanation.walkthrough: Firm suggests a business, but it is the adjective for solid.
explanation.definitionFit: A die-hard is a stubborn conservative who resists change and clings to established ways.

clue.text: What would supply bark, say?

parts.note: surface reading: whatever produces a yelp
setter's reading: a tree's outer covering, so a timber whose name begins with an animal that yelps

explanation.walkthrough: Both senses of bark are at work: the noise and the tree covering.
explanation.definitionFit: The dogwood is a flowering shrub or tree, so it has bark, and its first half is the animal that barks.

clue.text: Peaceful bird

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a kingfisher, in legend calming the sea while nesting

explanation.definitionFit: The word means calm and idyllic, and also names a kingfisher said in myth to still the winter waves.

clue.text: Plant in which one's typically found

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a garden flower with papery, translucent seed pods
second meaning: the virtue in which a person is normally found, and the letters of one's sit within the word too

explanation.walkthrough: A bonus: the answer literally contains one's, so the second half is also true of its spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: The plant Lunaria is called this for its see-through pods, and truthfulness is what one usually displays.

clue.text: Transport for players with jumpers on, hopefully

definitions.text: Transport for players with jumpers on, hopefully

parts.note: surface reading: a vehicle carrying musicians
setter's reading: opportunists leap aboard it hoping to share in success

explanation.walkthrough: Jumpers looks like knitwear the players are wearing; it means people who jump on board.
explanation.definitionFit: A cart carrying a band in a parade gave the idiom for joining a popular cause to gain from it.

clue.text: Roar half-heartedly in hell

indicators.note: half-heartedly takes away half of the middle, losing one of its central pair

parts.note: to roar is to bellow

explanation.surface: A damned soul roars weakly in the inferno.
explanation.walkthrough: The heart of the word is its doubled middle letter, and only half of it goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Down below is a euphemism for the underworld, so being there means being in the infernal regions.

clue.text: Sounds like keen member of school

indicators.note: sounds like says the answer is pronounced the same as the word that follows

parts.note: to keen is to wail in grief

explanation.surface: An eager pupil sounds like they belong at school.
explanation.walkthrough: Keen looks like eager; it is the verb for lamenting.
explanation.definitionFit: Whales swim in groups called schools, like fish.

clue.text: Drive mile, perhaps, without a sign of parking

indicators.note: without here means outside, so one piece wraps around the other
perhaps hints the word might be put another way, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
P is the road sign for a car park

explanation.surface: A motorist drives a mile looking in vain for a parking sign.
explanation.definitionFit: To impel is to drive or push forward, to force into motion.

clue.text: Would-be queen swallowing king's seafood

indicators.note: something swallowing takes another thing inside it

parts.note: a chess pawn reaching the far rank can be promoted to queen
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A royal hopeful eats the king's shellfish.
explanation.walkthrough: Would-be queen suggests a princess; it is a chess piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A prawn is a small shellfish eaten as seafood.

clue.text: Possesses a pound, initially, in capital

indicators.note: initially says this piece goes at the start, ahead of the others

parts.note: L, from Latin libra, is the pound sign
owns
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone has a pound to spend in the city.
explanation.walkthrough: Initially looks like a first-letter selection but it just positions the pound sign first.
explanation.definitionFit: Lhasa is the chief city of Tibet, seat of the Dalai Lama.

clue.text: One shows it by stubborn attitude or by actions, possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals that the words could be arranged in some other order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A mulish person displays it through attitude or deeds.
explanation.definitionFit: Obstinacy is pig-headedness, a refusal to change one's mind or give way.

clue.text: Occasion of woeful child's first appearance

definitions.text: Occasion of woeful child's first appearance

parts.words: Occasion of woeful child's first appearance
parts.note: surface reading: a sad infant's debut
setter's reading: the nursery rhyme says the child born on a certain weekday is full of woe, so the birthday is meant

explanation.walkthrough: The rhyme Monday's Child runs through the week, giving each day's baby a trait.
explanation.definitionFit: In the nursery rhyme, the child born on this midweek day is full of woe, so it is that baby's birth day.

clue.text: An academic or liberal type

parts.note: a don is a university teacher, especially at Oxford or Cambridge
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is either a university teacher or a political liberal.
explanation.walkthrough: Liberal seems political; it means generous.
explanation.definitionFit: A donor gives generously, and liberal can mean open-handed with money or gifts.
